decisions.reason: As a flagship digital workflow line tightly linked to the firm's core dental software and supported by in-house R&D, it fits existing knowledge and is highly improvable through customer learning.

The education institute uses the firm's training content and practitioner ties, so although it is less central than software, the firm can absorb feedback and refine it without stretching far beyond its knowledge base.

The remote support tool complements the firm's established support and integration capabilities, but because similar functions can be substituted by generic tools its retention is somewhat less certain than core software modules.
The analytics dashboard draws directly on the firm's installed software base and domain data, giving it strong relatedness and good scope for iterative improvement through R&D and user feedback.

A complete practice bundle is very close to the firm's existing modular offer and commercialization capabilities, so it is more likely to be retained as a packaging and cross-selling vehicle than withdrawn.

The job and practice listing portal relies on marketplace capabilities that are relatively distant from the firm's core software and support knowledge, so absorptive capacity is weaker and management is more likely to redeploy resources elsewhere.
